questions.text: In which of these 90's classics is the line spoken: 'In case I don't see you, good afternoon, good evening, good night!'?
questions.funfact: The line is Truman Burbank's signature sign-off, said throughout the show-within-the-show - fittingly used again as his final line when he walks off set at the end of the film.

questions.text: Which Premier League club has just been found guilty of all 115 charges of breaching financial rules over a 9-year period between 2009 and 2018?
questions.funfact: The charges covered alleged breaches from the 2009-10 season through to 2017-18, spanning financial fair play rules, profitability requirements, and failing to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

questions.text: Translated as 'the little boy' in Spanish, what is the name given to the natural climate pattern that increases warm ocean currents in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.funfact: Combined with long-term climate trends, this super El Nino has driven global ocean temperatures to historic highs, putting 2027 on track to potentially become the hottest year on record.

questions.text: The Gobi Desert stretches over China and which other country?
questions.funfact: The Gobi is Asia's largest desert, spanning roughly 1.3 million square kilometres across southern Mongolia and northern China.

questions.text: Where does a troglodyte live?
questions.funfact: The word comes from the Greek 'troglodytes', meaning 'one who creeps into holes' - historically used to describe cave-dwelling peoples.

questions.text: Where do pierogies traditionally come from?
questions.funfact: Pierogi have been a staple of Polish cuisine since the Middle Ages, though neighbouring Ukraine, Russia and Slovakia all have their own versions and some claim to the dish's origins too.

questions.text: Which celebrity is famous for the brand Fenty?
questions.funfact: Rihanna launched Fenty Beauty in 2017 with an unprecedented 40 foundation shades, widely credited with pushing the beauty industry toward better shade inclusivity.

questions.text: Where would you find your thyroid in the body?
questions.funfact: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland at the base of the neck that regulates metabolism by producing hormones

questions.text: What is the capital of Scotland?
questions.funfact: Despite Glasgow being Scotland's largest city, Edinburgh has been the capital since at least the 15th century and is home to the Scottish Parliament.

questions.text: Guess the year: Malala Yousafzai became the youngest-ever Nobel Peace Prize laureate, How I Met Your Mother aired its finale, and Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 mysteriously vanished over the Indian Ocean.
questions.funfact: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize at just 17 years old, sharing it with Indian children's rights activist Kailash Satyarthi.

questions.text: RSPCA - what does the C stand for?
questions.funfact: The RSPCA stands for the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, what does 'cooked' mean?
questions.funfact: 'Cooked' exploded in Gen Z slang via gaming and TikTok culture, meaning someone is finished, doomed, or about to fail spectacularly. For example 'bro is cooked' after a bad test.

questions.text: Which of the following TV shows had the most episodes?
questions.funfact: Friends ran for 10 seasons and 236 episodes, well ahead of The US Office's 201 (9 seasons), Seinfeld's 180 (9 seasons), and Parks and Recreation's 125 (7 seasons).

questions.text: The 2026 movie 'Tony' that has just been released is a biopic about which famous person? (Full name)
questions.funfact: Tony stars Dominic Sessa as the late chef, author and TV host, showing his experiences before writing his acclaimed Kitchen Confidential.

questions.text: Hydrogen and Helium are the first 2 elements of the Periodic Table, name the next 5 elements. (Hint: Initials are L, B, B, C, N)
questions.funfact: Lithium through Nitrogen make up elements 3 through 7 on the periodic table. Lithium is prized for batteries, while Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.text: What is the name of Taylor Swift's latest single, released last week, that shares its name with the technical term for the very first individual to contract a specific disease?
questions.funfact: The term is believed to stem from a mislabeling during 1980s AIDS research, when a Canadian flight attendant was labelled Patient 'O' (for 'Outside California') - later misread as the number zero.

questions.text: Complete the next 4 lyrics: 'Someday I'll wish upon a star / And wake up where the clouds are far behind me / Where troubles melt like lemon drops / Away...'
questions.funfact: This is 'Over the Rainbow' from The Wizard of Oz. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1939 and was later named the greatest movie song of all time by the American Film Institute.

questions.text: What is the name given to a squirrel's den?
questions.funfact: A drey is typically built high in tree forks from twigs, leaves and bark, and squirrels often maintain multiple dreys across their territory.

questions.text: Which of these is the biggest selling coffee brand by sales in the world?
questions.funfact: Nescafe's footprint is so vast that one out of every seven cups of coffee consumed worldwide is a Nescafé product

questions.text: Which one of these is not a pasta shape - Bucatini, Farfalle, Orecchiette, Stracciatella?
questions.funfact: Stracciatella is the Burrata Filling, the creamy, gooey centre that spills out when you cut open a ball of burrata. Bucatini is a long, thick noodle with a hollow centre running through it like a straw. Farfalle is bow-tie shaped pasta. Orecchiette means 'little ears' in Italian.

questions.text: Trypophobia is a fear of what?
options: Clusters of small holes or bumps
questions.funfact: Though not officially recognised as a clinical phobia, trypophobia sufferers report real feelings of disgust or unease when viewing clustered holes like lotus seed pods or honeycomb.

questions.text: Which country's name is spelled using the 7 most common letters in the English alphabet, once each?
questions.funfact: The most frequently used letters in English are roughly E, T, A, O, I, N, S - rearranged, they spell 'Estonia'

questions.text: What is the scientific or medical term for 'goosebumps'?
questions.funfact: Piloerection, Horripilation or Cutis anserina describe the same reflex: tiny muscles at the base of hair follicles contracting, a leftover survival response from when our ancestors had enough body hair for it to trap warmth or make them look bigger to predators.

questions.text: Which of the following foods is Kosher?
questions.funfact: Kosher dietary law (related to the Jewish religion) permits mammals that both chew cud and have cloven hooves (like goats and cows), while pork and shellfish are both forbidden - most insects, including crickets, are non-kosher too, with only a few specific locust species as an exception.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Talisia for this question!

questions.text: On a standard Rubik's Cube, how many small cubes can you actually see and touch on the outside of the cube?
questions.funfact: A Rubik's Cube has 27 small cubes total (3x3x3), but the very centre cube is completely hidden inside the mechanism with no stickers at all - leaving 26 you can see and touch: 8 corners, 12 edges, and 6 face centres.

questions.text: What movie is the following quote from? 'Ohana means family, and family means nobody gets left behind or forgotten.'
questions.funfact: 'Ohana' is the Hawaiian word for family. Stitch’s nasally, growly voice was provided by none other than his creator Chris Sanders.

questions.text: Which Colleen Hoover novel, similar to the French word for 'truth', has just been adapted for cinemas, starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett?
questions.funfact: Verity is a 2018 psychological thriller by Colleen Hoover, and the film adaptation hit cinemas in early October 2026. The title comes from the Latin 'veritas', meaning truth.

questions.text: What does the word 'Simian' mean?
questions.funfact: 'Simian' comes from the Latin 'simia', meaning ape. It describes anything to do with apes and monkeys - and humans are technically apes too.

questions.text: In what month does the original Oktoberfest in Munich always start?
questions.funfact: Despite the name, Oktoberfest begins in September and runs for 16-18 days, finishing on the first Sunday in October (or 3 October if that Sunday falls too early).

questions.text: Impressionism, Pop Art, Surrealism, Cubism - which of the following art movements is from the 1800s and NOT the 1900s?
questions.funfact: Impressionism (1860s-1880s, Monet and Degas) took its name from Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise'. Cubism began around 1907 with Picasso and Braque, Pop Art took off in the 1950s with Warhol, and Surrealism grew out following World War 1, through artists like Dali

questions.text: Which spice is made from the bark of a tree?
questions.funfact: Cinnamon comes from the inner bark of Cinnamomum trees. The bark is stripped, dried and naturally curls into the rolled 'quills' you see as cinnamon sticks.

questions.text: Which A-list celebrity sold his AI post-production startup, InterPositive, to Netflix for $587 million in cash?
questions.funfact: Affleck founded InterPositive in 2022 and ran it in stealth mode. Its tools let filmmakers train an AI model on their own footage to help with post-production like relighting shots, and Netflix's filing put the price at about $587 million.

questions.text: Which famous astronomer described Earth in the Pale Blue Dot photograph as a tiny, fragile speck of dust suspended in a sunbeam within a vast cosmic arena?
questions.funfact: Voyager 1 took the Pale Blue Dot photo in 1990 from roughly 6 billion kilometres away, where Earth takes up less than a single pixel. Sagan's reflection on it is one of the most quoted passages in science writing.

questions.text: Which is the only country in the world that has a flag with the front different from the back?
questions.funfact: Paraguay's flag shows the national coat of arms on the front and the Treasury seal on the back, which makes it the only national flag with two different sides.

questions.text: Guess the year: The Notebook was released, Google launched Gmail, and Janet Jackson and Justin Timberlake performed at the Super Bowl halftime show, sparking the massive 'Nipplegate' broadcast controversy.
questions.funfact: Gmail launched on 1 April 2004 offering a huge 1GB of storage, and many people assumed it was an April Fools' joke.

questions.text: RAM - what does the R in RAM stand for? (Related to Computers)
questions.funfact: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, because the computer can jump straight to any stored data without reading through it in order. The world is currently facing a severe RAM and memory crunch, driven largely by huge demand from AI data centres.

questions.text: In Gen Z text and online slang, what does 'FR' stand for?
questions.funfact: 'FR' is used to agree with something or to stress that you mean it, as in 'that movie was so good, fr'. It often gets extended to 'fr fr' for extra emphasis.

questions.text: On a dartboard, what score is the inner Bullseye worth (Red)?
questions.funfact: The red inner bull scores 50, while the green outer bull ring around it is worth 25. In darts the bullseye counts as a double, so it can be used to finish a game.

questions.text: Which movie title has had all of its vowels removed? 'THRWLLBBLD'
questions.funfact: There Will Be Blood (2007) was directed by Paul Thomas Anderson and is loosely based on Upton Sinclair's 1927 novel 'Oil!'. Daniel Day-Lewis won the Oscar for Best Actor for his role as Daniel Plainview.

questions.text: Name the 5 countries that border Switzerland.
questions.funfact: Switzerland is landlocked and shares its longest border with Italy and its shortest with tiny Liechtenstein. Liechtenstein is itself doubly landlocked, meaning every country it borders is landlocked too.

questions.text: In Don McLean's classic 'American Pie', he references 'the day the music died'. Which famous singer was he referring to?
questions.funfact: Buddy Holly died in a plane crash on 3 February 1959, aged just 22, alongside Ritchie Valens and The Big Bopper. McLean's 1971 anthem 'American Pie' cemented the date in folklore, and Holly's style inspired a generation including The Beatles, The Rolling Stones and Bob Dylan.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 words: 'Won't make my Mama proud, it's gonna cause a scene / She sees her baby girl, I know she's gonna scream / God, what have you done? / You're a pink pony girl, and...'
acceptedAnswers: And you dance at the club
questions.funfact: This is 'Pink Pony Club' by Chappell Roan. Released in 2020, it became a breakout hit in 2024 and helped her win Best New Artist at the 2025 Grammys.

questions.text: Which type of animal has had a new species identified in Bolivia?
questions.funfact: The new species, Leopardus tilcayo, is a tiny tiger cat about 46cm long and weighing just 1.4-2kg, found in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest. It is the first new living cat species identified in more than 100 years, and genetic analysis showed it split from other tiger cats about 1.4 million years ago.

questions.text: Which media company has just completed its acquisition of the movie studio Warner Bros?
questions.funfact: Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery closed on 6 October 2026, and the combined company is now called Skydance, trading on the New York Stock Exchange as SKYD. It brings together CBS, HBO, CNN and franchises like Harry Potter and Top Gun.

questions.text: Odd one out: Which one does Meta not own - Instagram, Twitch, WhatsApp, Threads
questions.funfact: Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads are all owned by Meta, while Twitch is owned by Amazon, which bought it in 2014 for around $970 million.

questions.text: What unusual shape is wombat poop?
questions.funfact: Wombats are the only known animal to produce cube-shaped poo, and they can make 80-100 pieces a night. They stack the cubes on rocks and logs to mark their territory, and the flat sides stop them from rolling away.

questions.text: A cat, a golf course, and things you copy and paste. What homophone can fit all three?
questions.funfact: A lynx is a wild cat, a golf course is called a links, and the hyperlinks you copy and paste are links too. The golfing term comes from the Old English 'hlinc', meaning ridge or rising ground, describing the sandy Scottish coastland where golf began.

questions.text: HAL 9000 is the artificial intelligence in the sci-fi epic 2001: A Space Odyssey. Which computer company is its name said to pay homage to? (Hint: Think Initials)
questions.funfact: Shift each letter of HAL forward by one and you get IBM. Author Arthur C. Clarke and director Stanley Kubrick always insisted it was a coincidence, and said HAL stood for Heuristically programmed ALgorithmic computer.

questions.text: Four sovereign countries have national anthems that are purely instrumental and have no official lyrics to sing. Can you name one?
questions.correctAnswer: Spain, Bosnia, San Marino or Kosovo
questions.funfact: Spain's 'Marcha Real', Bosnia and Herzegovina's 'Intermezzo', San Marino's 'Inno Nazionale' and Kosovo's 'Europe' are all wordless. Kosovo chose an instrumental anthem on purpose so it wouldn't favour the language of any one ethnic group.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Talisia for this question!

questions.text: What is the largest number less than 1,000,000 that doesn't contain the letter R when spelled out in words? (Digits only, no commas)
questions.funfact: 99,099 is 'ninety-nine thousand and ninety-nine', which has no R anywhere. Anything with a hundreds part fails because 'hundred' contains an R, so the thousands part can't go above ninety-nine.

questions.text: What movie is the following quote from? 'Parting your soup is not a miracle, it's a magic trick. ... You want to see a miracle, son? Be the miracle.'
questions.funfact: The line is spoken by Morgan Freeman, who plays God in Bruce Almighty (2003) opposite Jim Carrey. The film grossed over $480 million worldwide, making it one of Carrey's biggest hits.

questions.text: Which country has been invited to become the EU's first associate member?
questions.funfact: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made the invitation in her State of the Union speech on 16 September 2026, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in the room. Canada isn't a European state so it can't be a full member, and the details of what associate membership would involve are still to be worked out.

questions.text: Which of the following is the Mandarin word for cat?
questions.funfact: The Mandarin word for cat is 猫 (māo), which sounds a lot like the 'meow' noise a cat makes.

questions.text: How many kilometres is a Parkrun event?
questions.funfact: Parkrun began in 2004 at Bushy Park in London with just 13 runners. It is now a free, timed 5km run held every Saturday morning in more than 20 countries, including hundreds of locations across Australia.

questions.text: Which of these ages lasted the longest?
questions.funfact: The Middle Ages ran from roughly 500 to 1500 AD, about 1,000 years. The Renaissance lasted about 300 years (c. 1300-1600), the 20th century was 100 years, and the Victorian Era, the reign of Queen Victoria from 1837 to 1901, was only about 64 years.

questions.text: What is the classic flavour of Turkish Delight?
questions.funfact: Turkish Delight, or lokum, has been made in Istanbul for more than 200 years, and rose is the classic flavour. It is also the sweet that tempted Edmund in C.S. Lewis's 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe'.

questions.text: Which famous pop star is married to New Zealand actor and director Taika Waititi?
questions.funfact: Rita Ora was born in Pristina, Kosovo, and moved to London with her family as a baby. Taika Waititi directed Thor: Ragnarok and won an Oscar for his screenplay for Jojo Rabbit.

questions.text: Are you taller in the morning or in the evening?
questions.funfact: You are usually about 1-2cm taller in the morning. Gravity squashes the discs in your spine during the day, and they slowly re-expand while you lie down and sleep.

questions.text: Which country is the only country in the world named after an element? (Hint: Might not be English)
questions.funfact: Argentina takes its name from the Latin 'argentum', meaning silver.

questions.text: Guess the year: the Beirut explosion in Lebanon, Kobe Bryant died in a helicopter crash, and the Pixar classic Soul was released.
questions.funfact: Kobe Bryant died on 26 January 2020, the Beirut port explosion happened on 4 August 2020, and Soul arrived on Disney+ on Christmas Day 2020 after cinemas were closed by the pandemic.

questions.text: Control + F on a Windows keyboard - what does the F stand for?
questions.funfact: Ctrl+F opens the Find box so you can search a page or document for a word. It works in almost every browser and app, and Ctrl+H opens Find + Replace.

questions.text: Complete the saying: 'Brevity is the soul of...'
questions.funfact: The line comes from Shakespeare's Hamlet, spoken by the long-winded Polonius, which is a joke in itself because he takes ages to get to the point.

questions.text: Which of the following hands will win in Texas Hold'em?
questions.funfact: From weakest to strongest these hands rank: three of a kind, straight, flush, full house. A full house is three of a kind plus a pair, which is why it beats the others.

questions.text: Who wrote the famous book 'The Grapes of Wrath'?
questions.funfact: John Steinbeck published The Grapes of Wrath in 1939 and it won the Pulitzer Prize in 1940. He went on to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1962.

questions.text: There are 10 countries in the world with 4 letters. Iran, Iraq, Fiji, Laos and Oman are 5 of them. Name the other 5 countries.
questions.funfact: The other five are Chad, Cuba, Mali, Peru and Togo. Chad takes its name from Lake Chad, and Peru is home to Machu Picchu.

questions.text: True or False: the lead singer of the band Blur also created the virtual band Gorillaz?
questions.funfact: Damon Albarn fronts Blur and co-created Gorillaz in 1998 with artist Jamie Hewlett. The 'band' is made up of cartoon characters 2-D, Murdoc, Noodle and Russel.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 words: 'Because of you / I never stray too far from the sidewalk / Because of you / I learned to play on the safe side...'
questions.funfact: This is 'Because of You' by Kelly Clarkson, from her 2004 album Breakaway. She co-wrote it, and has said it was inspired by her parents' divorce.

questions.text: What type of bird was traditionally taken down into coal mines to warn miners of dangerous gas?
questions.funfact: Canaries are far more sensitive to toxic gases like carbon monoxide than humans are, so if the bird stopped singing or collapsed, the miners knew to get out. British mines used canaries until 1986.

questions.text: Which movie title has had all of its vowels removed? 'THBLRWTCHPRJCT'
questions.funfact: The Blair Witch Project (1999) was made for a reported $60,000 and went on to gross nearly $250 million, helping launch the found-footage horror genre.

questions.text: Odd one out: Lorraine, Bourguignon, Carcassonne, Roquefort. Three of these French places give their name to a food or dish. Which one doesn't?
questions.funfact: Dijon gives its name to mustard, Bourguignon (Burgundy) to the beef stew boeuf bourguignon, and Brie to the cheese. Carcassonne is a medieval walled city in southern France with 52 towers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997 also the name of a popular Board Game

questions.text: What is the name of the cat that chases Tweety Bird in Looney Tunes?
questions.funfact: Sylvester and Tweety first teamed up in 'Tweetie Pie' (1947), which won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short. Tweety was originally pink, until censors thought he looked too naked and the animators changed him to yellow.

questions.text: What letter comes next in the sequence: M, V, E, M, J, S, U ...?
questions.funfact: The letters are the first letters of the planets in order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, so next comes Neptune. Neptune was found in 1846 after mathematicians predicted its position.

questions.text: Iambic pentameter is a common rhythmic meter in English poetry. What is the rhythm supposed to mirror or resemble?
questions.funfact: Each line has five da-DUM pairs, which sounds like a heartbeat. Shakespeare used it constantly, as in 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?'

questions.text: What is the longest Harry Potter movie?
questions.funfact: Chamber of Secrets (2002) runs for 161 minutes, just ahead of Goblet of Fire at 157 minutes and Half-Blood Prince at 153 minutes. The shortest is Deathly Hallows Part 2 at 130 minutes.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Dan for this question!

questions.text: What is the answer to this sum? 6 + 4 ÷ 2 + 3 × 3
questions.funfact: Multiplication and division come before addition, so it becomes 6 + 2 + 9 = 17.
